slot.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slot.brief: Rank alkenes by heat of hydrogenation / stability (cis-trans-substituted comparison); pick correct increasing or decreasing order

stem: Which sequence gives the alkenes in increasing order of heat of hydrogenation?

verdicts.working: More substituted and less strained alkenes are more stable, so they release less heat on hydrogenation. Stability order: trans-2-butene > cis-2-butene > propene > ethene; therefore heat of hydrogenation increases in the reverse order.

working:
Alkene stability: trans-2-butene > cis-2-butene > propene > ethene.
Heat of hydrogenation is inversely related to alkene stability.
Therefore: trans-2-butene < cis-2-butene < propene < ethene.

Independent check: More substituted and less strained alkenes are more stable, so they release less heat on hydrogenation. Stability order: trans-2-butene > cis-2-butene > propene > ethene; therefore heat of hydrogenation increases in the reverse order.
solution:
Heat of hydrogenation is inversely proportional to alkene stability. The stability order is trans-2-butene > cis-2-butene > propene > ethene; hence the increasing order of heat of hydrogenation is
$$\text{trans-2-butene} < \text{cis-2-butene} < \text{propene} < \text{ethene}$$
